WHAT CHANGED SINCE v59 ON THIS TARGET -- THREE COMPILER FIXES, ALL TARGET-INDEPENDENT
  This target goes straight from v59 to v62, so it takes v60, v61 and v62 at once.
  git diff --stat 5c89c538b8 ade0c47fc4 -- compiler/ is exactly fmodule.pas +32,
  nbas.pas +19, tgobj.pas +15; nothing under rtl/ or packages/ moved.
    407ef9bb3a  GOD   (v60)  tgobj.pas  a freed statement-scoped interface temp is
                re-stamped to the statement that freed it, so the prefix temps of
                "with Make do begin ... end" no longer leak until routine exit.
    2df7b40d2a  Otto  (v61)  nbas.pas   a compiler-built statement list is never
                spliced into a source block.  "with Make.o do begin ... end" (Make
                returns a COM interface, .o the object inside it) released the
                interface BEFORE the body ran whenever the with statement was not
                the first statement of its block -- the body worked on a FREED
                object.  A use-after-free on every target, at -O- and -O2.
    ade0c47fc4  Otto  (v62)  fmodule.pas  a unit compiled FROM SOURCE is recompiled,
                not reloaded, when a unit it resolved symbols out of is reset in
                the middle of a build.  The reload left pointers into the freed
                unit; incremental Lazarus IDE builds died with EAccessViolation
                (exit 217).  Measured on v59, v60 and v61 before the fix.
  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change,
  so the unit set this target already pairs with stays valid.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES -- BY RUNNING THEM, WITH THE PUBLISHED v59 AS THE CONTROL
  * Four self-checking programs from tests/test/ were compiled BY THIS BINARY
    against the PUBLISHED unit set this target pairs with, and the products
    RAN (natively -- this x86_64 host runs 32-bit i386 code):
      tintfstmttemp1    -O- checks=32 fails=0 created=25
                        -O2 checks=32 fails=0 created=25
      tintfstmttemp2    -O- checks=28 fails=0 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0
                        -O2 checks=28 fails=0 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0
      tintfwithprefix1  -O- checks=62 fails=0 created=56 destroyed=56 live=0
                        -O2 checks=62 fails=0 created=56 destroyed=56 live=0
      tintflifetime1    -O- checks=28 fails=0
                        -O2 checks=28 fails=0
    tintfstmttemp1/2 cover v59's statement-end release, tintfwithprefix1 the
    v60 + v61 with-statement fixes, tintflifetime1 the four published
    interface lifetime rules.
  * THE CONTROL SAYS NO: the published v59 binary for this target (md5 880fe174bee5b180b82530a4b13c6185),
    run through the identical harness, scores
      tintfwithprefix1  -O- checks=62 fails=16 created=56 destroyed=55 live=1
                        -O2 checks=62 fails=16 created=56 destroyed=55 live=1
    so the pass above is a measurement, not a harness that cannot fail.
  * dist/ppu-reload-check.sh (the v62 fix, scored on the compiler's own -vu
    text): RESULT: PASS on this binary; the v59 control: RESULT: FAIL.
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh against the published units/i386-linux/aspelldyn.ppu:
    25/25 offsets clean (run with TRUNCCHECK_VMCAP_KB=8388608).
  * dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh was NOT run for this target: no tree on this box
    holds a packages/*/units/i386-linux unit set today (the published set is one flat
    units/ dir), and none was rebuilt to manufacture one.  The programs above
    were compiled against the published set itself.

NOT PROVEN HERE: nobody has run this compiler, or anything it emits, on a 32-bit
i386 INSTALL.  The generated programs ran on x86_64-linux, which executes i386
code natively; that covers codegen and RTL, not a real 32-bit userland.
